facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old man
recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of his right thumb
four-year history of a lesion at that site
partial amputation of the thumb was performed in December 2016
the lesion reappeared at the distal aspect of the thumb stump
no significant medical history
took no medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, indurated lesion
no palpable lymphadenopathy was noted
enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease

concepts.why: The patient has a recurrent skin lesion with a four-year history, and the lesion is described as well-circumscribed, firm, and indurated, which are characteristic features of squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient has a skin lesion that is well-circumscribed and firm, which could be consistent with basal cell carcinoma, although the presence of metastatic disease makes this less likely.
The patient has a recurrent skin lesion with metastatic disease, which could be consistent with Merkel cell carcinoma, a highly aggressive type of skin cancer.
The patient has a skin lesion with metastatic disease, which could be consistent with melanoma, although the description of the lesion does not specifically suggest this diagnosis.
